prompt: Review the checkout summary widget added in PR 3307. It is a small browser-only storefront change, and I want confidence before this reaches the next checkout release because it is a new customer-facing path. Read the project context and the PR materials under `pr/3307/`, including the changed files and the surrounding modules and docs they rely on. Write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project. Keep findings concrete and tied to the code, with a severity and a developer-ready fix for each issue. End the review with a fenced json list of findings, each with `location` (`path/to/file.ext:LINE`, with line numbers of the file as it is in the project), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);let n=0;for(const x of L)for(const m of String(x.location).matchAll(/([A-Za-z0-9_.\/-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+):(\d+)/g)){n++;let c;try{c=fs.readFileSync(m[1],"utf8").split("\n").length}catch{process.exit(1)}if(+m[2]<1||+m[2]>c)process.exit(1)}process.exit(n?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Fail: the review omits important concrete consequences, gives fixes that a developer cannot act on, or invents issues unsupported by this project. Partial: the review identifies some real risks but explains consequences or fixes inconsistently. Pass: each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on without adding unsupported concerns (code cannot check this because the quality of reasoning and project-specific explanation are not mechanically observable)

findingsKey.finding: The promotion input has no associated visible label, and invalid input is communicated only by changing the color of the input and hint while the status remains empty, so keyboard and color-blind users do not get an accessible error or field relationship.
Each promotion keystroke calls renderLines, which adds another click listener to the same list after replacing its children, causing handlers to accumulate during normal typing.

The widget converts catalog cents to a floating point price and then builds currency strings with toFixed and a dollar prefix, so the fr-FR and de-DE locales documented for checkout cannot format separators and symbols correctly and floating point totals can leak into the UI.
Both service messages are assigned to innerHTML, allowing a promotion or order response containing markup from the server to execute script in the checkout page.
The submit handler has no in-flight guard or disabled state, so two rapid clicks can send two order requests even though the checkout contract requires one request per user action.
The action is labeled Place order even though the checkout copy rule requires the imperative button label Submit order, making the new control inconsistent with the documented UI text.

verdicts.note: Prompt asks for general code review without naming methods, checklists, or hinting at specific problems.
Clear instructions: review PR 3307, write findings to REVIEW.md with severity and fixes, output JSON.
Some items require deeper analysis (event listener accumulation, currency formatting across files); not all would be caught in quick shallow review.
All key items are findable from code and documentation; line numbers match; severities defensible.
No comments, tests, or filenames point directly at planted issues. Documentation states correct practices without highlighting violations.
